data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002 carries the single-difference mutation and minimal-fixture principle into its analogy and transfer claims, and it is clearly intended to cover both requirements (its analogy disanalogies explicitly note 'no coverage-counting counterpart to the school-to-seat binding problem'). Yet the claim itself only instantiates the forbidden-case mutation for the typed lease-mismatch code -> generic 500 / fall-through success path. It never names the specific single-difference mutation for the coverage-counting refusal: i.e., a suite that silently passes when a school-to-seat binding whose endpoint identity disagrees with the frozen seat IS counted as coverage (mutating the coverage predicate from `reject` to `accept` while leaving the frozen-seat fixture untouched). The problem requires the skeleton's forbidden cases to EACH name a mutation that would today pass the suite silently, and for the school-to-seat case the relevant silent-pass mutation is coverage miscounting, not code genericization. By folding only the lease-mismatch mutation into its concrete claim while leaving the coverage mutation as an unaddressed disanalogy, SRC_002 under-specifies the forbidden case for requirement (2) and thus fails the problem's deliverable standard for that refusal.
